coverage_gaps: No current primary-source filings were reviewed in this Layer 1A call; company-specific claims require 10-K/20-F/annual report, investor presentation, earnings-call, and customer-disclosure verification.

The supplied external context is mostly secondary research and snippets; stronger evidence is needed from company filings, industry standards bodies, procurement records, and customer capex disclosures.

Cybersecurity and automation were included as hypothesis lanes because the theme query requires them, but the provided evidence set is much stronger for AI semiconductors, packaging, photonics, and data-center infrastructure.
No market-pricing check was performed; later layers should compare revenue exposure, market cap, analyst coverage, valuation, short interest, and recent price discovery.
Customer/supplier dependency remains unverified for most underfollowed nodes; later work should test whether suppliers are actually sole/limited-source or easily substitutable.

memory_update.text: For broad Technology research, separate obvious AI semiconductor demand from second-order bottlenecks in packaging materials, optics tools, power/cooling/grid infrastructure, specialized AI cloud capacity, and semiconductor data orchestration.
Advanced packaging substrate yield, ABF-style insulating materials, and copper-bonding chemistry are priority underfollowed nodes for AI semiconductor supply-chain discovery.
Compound semiconductor epitaxy and photonics manufacturing tools are a promising underfollowed node tied to AI optical interconnect scaling.
Semiconductor manufacturing data/orchestration software is a potential software chokepoint as chiplet and advanced packaging workflows span fabless, foundry, OSAT, and test ecosystems.
AI data-center power, cooling, transformer, switchgear, and grid-interconnection suppliers should be tracked as physical infrastructure bottlenecks rather than generic industrials.
Cybersecurity and automation remain under-sourced in the current evidence set and require focused primary-source searches before company mapping.

layer1a.summary: Technology is too broad to research as one theme. A Serenity Layer 1A decomposition should split it into AI compute demand, semiconductor complexity, optical/data-center connectivity, physical data-center infrastructure, cloud/AI capacity, and software/control-plane dependencies. The highest-quality discovery lanes are likely one or two layers below the obvious mega-cap beneficiaries: advanced packaging materials and substrates, compound semiconductor and photonics tools, semiconductor data/orchestration software, AI data-center power/cooling/grid equipment, specialized AI-cloud capacity, and cybersecurity/automation infrastructure exposed to rising machine-driven workloads. This is an initial decomposition, not a security recommendation.

supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer USD 300M-10B substrate or specialty material companies; allow larger names only if the advanced-packaging exposure is unusually direct. Screen out diversified conglomerates where AI package exposure is immaterial.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders only to define demand and capex direction: NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, hyperscalers, and large cloud/software platforms. Lane 2 hunts underfollowed public suppliers one or two layers below them: substrates, insulating film, wet chemistry, epitaxy tools, optical component suppliers, semiconductor analytics/orchestration software, data-center electrical equipment, power conversion, cooling components, testing/inspection, identity/security tooling, observability, and industrial automation software. Prefer USD 300M-10B market caps where plausible, allow USD 10B-30B only for unusually pure exposure, and treat micro-caps as speculative exceptions requiring strong evidence checks.
supply_side_constraints: HBM and advanced packaging capacity, with downstream constraints shifting into substrates, insulating films, copper-bonding chemistry, and package yield
Optical interconnect scaling, including lasers, compound semiconductor wafers, epitaxy capacity, and deposition tools
